quarterly_data.signal: BACKLOG INCREASE SIZED EX-FRONTIER-LABS: Bill Duff, CFO of Microsoft's Global Commercial Sales and Marketing business, said that when Microsoft announced last quarter's results it 'saw an increase in our backlog of about $50 billion, a little bit more than $50 billion' and that this increase was ALL OUTSIDE OpenAI and Anthropic - i.e. entirely non-Frontier-lab, and still growing. (The Q4 FY2026 call had already said ALL sequential RPO growth came from customers outside the frontier-model companies; the ~$50 billion size of that increase, and the explicit inclusion of Anthropic alongside OpenAI, is what is new. His Foundry proxy - 'over 100,000 customers who have doubled revenue' year-over-year, spread across geographies and segments rather than concentrated - repeats the Q4 FY2026 disclosure.)
quarterly_data.figure: an increase in our backlog of about $50 billion, a little bit more than $50 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CAPACITY ALLOCATION MECHANIC: Duff said Microsoft runs a 'common architecture' - external Azure AI customers, Microsoft's own first-party services and Copilots, and internal R&D all sit on the EXACT SAME infrastructure, so capacity can be dynamically rebalanced across those three uses to match supply to demand, and efficiency gains in first-party services free capacity for Azure customers. Allocation starts from customer commitments; he expects 'demand will continue to be greater than supply through the remainder of this calendar year' - a line he explicitly attributed to Amy Hood's recent earnings commentary, so the supply/demand call itself is a restatement and the common-architecture rebalancing mechanic is the new part.
quarterly_data.figure: demand will continue to be greater than supply through the remainder of this calendar year
